attack_description: Ran the existing, unmodified acceptance probe amphora-assurance-capabilities/tests/cf_packet_repair_content_binding_probe.rs (authored 2026-08-11 as the intended CF-PACKET fire-2 acceptance test but never signed into a receipt or logged to the falsification ledger) twice (two-replay, byte-identical JSON output). The probe drafts a final-assembly packet whose candidate_binding.blueprint_citations[0].sha256 is set to a fabricated value ('f'*64) that does not match the real amphora-report-packager/reference/mvp20/out/blueprint.md bytes, then checks validate(), sign(), verify_signature() against an honest TrustStore, and the separate disk-bound verify_blueprint_citations(root) gate.
claim_under_attack: CroProtocolPackageV2::sign()/verify_signature() (the DSSE Ed25519 signing boundary) establish that a final-assembly packet's locked_numeric_thresholds are content-bound to the blueprint artifacts cited in candidate_binding.blueprint_citations, per the CF-PACKET done_criterion clause and the verify_blueprint_citations doc comment in amphora-assurance-capabilities/src/lib.rs
does_not_close: Does not claim verify_blueprint_citations(root) itself is broken -- it correctly detects the mismatch when called; the gap is that sign()/verify_signature() never call it.

Does not claim any currently-shipped packet in this module's reference/ or evidence/ trees actually carries a fabricated blueprint citation -- this is a capability gap in the runtime API, demonstrated with a constructed test packet, not a claim about existing signed artifacts.

Does not itself repair the gap (e.g. by having verify_signature() take an optional root: Option<&Path> and call verify_blueprint_citations when locked_numeric_thresholds is non-empty); that is a follow-on repair-item fire.
No CRO acceptance, wet-lab, qualification, procurement, or release authority; no promotion, manifest edit, KPI/benchmark-lock edit, or scientific_readiness flip.
finding: CLAIM_REFUTED (residual, distinct from CF-PACKET fire 1). The 2026-08-11 CF-PACKET repair added structural blueprint-citation presence checks to validate() and a new disk-bound verify_blueprint_citations(root) gate that correctly re-derives and compares each cited blueprint's sha256 against its real bytes. But sign() and verify_signature() -- the module's actual DSSE Ed25519 cryptographic-authenticity boundary, the one this portfolio's SIGNING DISCIPLINE treats as authoritative everywhere else -- call validate() only and NEVER call verify_blueprint_citations(root). Consequently a packet whose blueprint_citations[0].sha256 is fabricated (does not match the real blueprint.md bytes) still validate()s Ok, sign()s Ok, and independently verify_signature()s Ok against an honest TrustStore; only a separately-named, easily-omitted extra call (verify_blueprint_citations(root), which needs the caller to also pass a filesystem root -- something sign()/verify_signature() do not take as an argument at all) detects the mismatch. A downstream consumer who follows this module's own documented pattern elsewhere (trust a valid DSSE signature as the authenticity/content-binding boundary; see T-02/W-CRO1's protocol_lock_sha256 precedent, which IS enforced inside validate()) will accept a cryptographically 'valid', signed CRO protocol packet whose locked numeric thresholds cite a blueprint hash that does not correspond to any real blueprint content. The done_criterion clause 'the packet citing every blueprint artifact by path+sha256 so the thresholds are content-bound to the blueprint they came from' is therefore still not established by the packet's own signature -- it is established only if the caller remembers an extra, differently-shaped, filesystem-dependent function call outside the signing/verification API.
